newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mortgage-backeds slide after Chicago PMI.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mortgage-backeds slide after Chicago PMI.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backed securities tumbled with Treasuries on Friday after reports showed manufacturing activity remains robust.
Pass-throughs slipped 6/32 to 19/32 in thin afternoon trading, traders said. The market was set for a recommended early close at 1400 EDT/1800 GMT.
One trader said he saw "some selling in current coupons from some guys who were re-hedging positions."
"I saw some selling early, but it was pretty light," another trader said. "Coupon spreads widened out a bid, as you would expect in this kind of market."
While the mortgage spread curve widened, spreads narrowed a few basis points over Treasury yields.

On Friday afternoon, Ginnie Mae 30-year 8.0 percent coupons were off 15/32 at 99-29/32, yielding 114 basis points over 10-year Treasuries. Comparable FNMAs were off 13/32 at 99-30/32, and FHLMCs were off 12/32 at 100-01/32.

Mortgage-backeds dipped after the Purchasing Management Association of Chicago (PMAC) said its index of manufacturing activity jumped to 60.0 in August from 51.2 in July, the sharpest increase since February 1995.
A report on factory orders, released at the same time, showed manufacturing orders rose 1.8 percent in July after a revised June decline of 0.7 percent.

The August employment report tops next week's economic calendar, economists said in a Reuters poll on Friday. On average, 23 experts forecast non-farm payrolls rose 244,000 in August after a 193,000 rise in July.
They projected a dip in the unemployment rate to 5.3 percent and a three-tenths uptick in average hourly earnings.
The market will be closed on Monday, September 2 for the Labor Day holiday.
